JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

WARNING:
The
Youth Protection Act
forbids the
publishing or broadcasting of information allowing for a child or the child’s
parents to be identified. Any person who contravenes this provision commits
an offence and is liable to a fine (sections 11.2, 11.2.1 and
135 Y.P.A.).

introduction

[
1
]

The Director is requesting that the security and
development of X be declared still in danger.

[
2
]

Today the Director is recommending that X be entrusted
to a rehabilitation center for a period of two years, that the contacts between
X and her mother be determined by the Director in terms of modalities,
frequency and supervision, taking notice that the frequency will diminish
progressively, with a social follow up for the same period.

[
3
]

It is to be noted that it has been difficult to
proceed in this case. No less than 4 times were the parties in court, twice it
was postponed and the actual hearing started January 31
st
2018, and
continued on May 23
rd
. On March 28
th
2018, it was
impossible to proceed because the day before, the child had a crisis and was in
distress and the worker had to be by her side.

[
4
]

Also, the Director has been hesitating to
recommend a one or two year order. He has changed his position throughout these
proceedings form one to the other and back.

[
5
]

The mother contests the duration of the order
seeked by the Director and wishes to be better informed about the frequency of
her contacts which she would prefer not to be diminished.

[
6
]

The father is absent. His coordinates are
unknown and he has not played an active part in the child’s life for some years.
The court proceeds in his absence

[
7
]

The child’s lawyer, after hearing the evidence, feels
a one year order would better answer X’s needs particularly since it is not
sure that she will remain at A. Furthermore, we need to have the complete
Trauma assessment that will only be available on June 6
th
, 2018.

Question in litigation

[
8
]

Do the recommended measures answer the needs of
the child and are they in her best interest?

Events since last court order

[
9
]

The Director is requesting that the court revise
the order rendered on December 8
th
, 2016 by the Honourable judge
Julie Beauchesne, by which she ordered that X remain entrusted to a
readaptation center for a period of one year. The order also allowed contacts
with her mother under the modalities and frequency determined by the Director.

[
10
]

Since the last court order, X remained at the A
group home in City A where she has been placed since May 2015.

[
11
]

This readaptation center answers her many
particular needs by an adapted program.

[
12
]

X was diagnosed with ADHD and oppositional
defiant disorder with provocation.

[
13
]

She receives a regular medical follow up with
her child psychiatrists Dr Bourget and Dr Petitpas and she takes medication.

[
14
]

Dr Petitpas produced a letter (D-13) in which
she also explains about her attachment vulnerability. She recommends a tight
follow up with a professional in City A who will develop with her a secure
therapeutic relationship.

[
15
]

In April 2018, X was evaluated at the Child Psychiatry
Department of the Jewish General Hospital. Dr. Judith Vogel added to X’s
diagnosis as she found that the child has a severe reactive attachment disorder
and likely multiple learning disabilities. Her behaviours highly suggests
Post-traumatic stress disorder which requires an independent evaluation.

[
16
]

She has revised her medication which needs to be
overseen carefully.

[
17
]

She needs constant surveillance as she puts
herself at risk on a regular basis and can be very impulsive.

[
18
]

For example, she has a tendency to run away from
the group home or the school.

[
19
]

She has obsessive behaviours, arranging and
rearranging objects in her surroundings. She functions better when she has
one-on-one accompaniment.

[
20
]

She also exhibits aggressive behaviour and
becomes physically abusive with staff and peers when she does not get what she
wants to the point where staff need to physically restrain her. This can happen
several times per month. She shows no remorse when she is confronted with the harm
she does.

[
21
]

She steals frequently and her knap sac has to be
searched on a regular basis. She uses vulgar language. She has attention
seeking behaviour.

[
22
]

She has difficulty with her sleeping patterns in
that she has difficulty in falling asleep and needs reassurance from staff. She
has also experienced nightmares and night walking, waking up and disturbing the
other children in the group home.

[
23
]

X has made many gains in terms of language
development, catching up with her language disorder.

[
24
]

Her schooling remains a problem. She had been
attending school in an adapted academic program but exhibits important
difficulties.

[
25
]

She can be aggressive with her peers and school
staff and can get very agitated.

[
26
]

She has been transported to the [organism A] (secure
environment) quite a few time to calm her down.

[
27
]

The school has then decided to provide her with
a safe place within their walls where she can go when she feels anxious. They
also provide the support of an educator who supports her through the day.

[
28
]

At some point, she started to refuse to go
school and was home schooled by a tutor.

[
29
]

In all circumstances, X needs great structure
and very steady routine to cope with her anxiety.

[
30
]

In February 2018, she was provided with a shadow
accompaniment at the group home. Although this helps her with her routine, it
is not the complete solution for X who still exhibits problematic behaviour.

[
31
]

The least change in her routine can provoke a
pattern of disorganisation.

[
32
]

The mother has been regular in her visits to X
but she missed a few supervised visits due to illness or lack of
transportation. During the first 9 months of 2017, X had weekly contacts with
her mother (phone calls and visits alternating each week). X appreciates the
mother / child contacts and misses her mom in between visits.

[
33
]

Starting September 2017, the visits were spaced
once every 3 weeks, as the mother had difficulty attending visits once every 2
weeks. X reacted negatively to the change.

[
34
]

Nonetheless, the mother missed several
supervised visits. She explains that this was due to difficulties with her
pregnancy.

[
35
]

In reaction, X has been more and more
aggressive. In fact, since April 2018, she has been more disorganized and
aggressive and had to be brought to the [organism A].

[
36
]

X is currently experiencing memories from her
past and fears that C (mother’s ex-partner) will find her.

[
37
]

The mother’s personal situation has improved.

[
38
]

In April 2017, the mother separated from her
partner Mr. C. After the separation, she reported being the victim of theft,
harassment and vandalism from her this man.

[
39
]

After experiencing some financial difficulties
following this, she progressively reorganised her personal life.

[
40
]

She is now in a relationship with another
partner, D. She gave birth to their daughter on February 28
th
2018.
It is her 7
th
child. They all have been placed through the social
services’ intervention.

[
41
]

She has been offering very good collaboration
with the Director and participates actively to the social follow up. Although
she has not been transparent about her pregnancy.

[
42
]

She has been following through her participation
in [organism A] activities.

The appropriate measures

[
43
]

It is clear from the evidence that X still needs
the support of a readaptation setting. But the duration requested seems very
long for such a young child (9 years old on 1
st
, 2018), especially
since she has been there already for the last 3 years.

[
44
]

The Court grants an order for one year during
which the Director will need to reflect on this child’s life plan.

[
45
]

The Court insists that a placement in a group
home cannot be a life plan for a child.

[
46
]

To this effect, the Court also noted the
recommendation from Dr Vogel from the Jewish General Hospital: « the
priority in this case should be the establishment and maintenance of a steady
home and interpersonal environment to allow for the gradual stabilization of X’s
severely dysregulated attachment » (D-16).

[
47
]

X is very preoccupied with her future and needs
to be reassured as to where she will be living until she reaches age of
majority. Especially since she is the only child at A amongst the children that
were placed at the same time that she was, who has not found a home.

[
48
]

Furthermore, the current children presently at city
A are mostly boys. Some threaten X which created a new concerning situation.

[
49
]

As for contacts with her mother, their frequency
and modalities have to take in consideration X’s best interest. She still nourishes
the hope of returning home, but the Director feels the prognosis of this
happening is rather grim.

[
50
]

In that regard, the professionals involved must
be consulted and their recommendations followed.

[
51
]

The present judgement completes and confirms each
and every observations that were made on the bench in presence of the parties.

FOR ALL THESE MOTIVES THE COURT:

GRANTS
the present application;

DECLARES
that the security and
development of the child X are still in danger;

PROLONGS
the Court order rendered on
December 8, 2016 in the present file;

ORDERS
that the child X be entrusted to
an institution operating a rehabilitation center for a period of one year;

ORDERS
that the contacts between the
child and her mother be determined by the Director of Youth Protection
concerning the terms, the frequency and the level of supervision;

RECOMMANDS
that the Director gives some
leeway in terms of frequency and modalities of contacts;

TAKE NOTICE
that the frequency of the
contacts between the child and her mother will be modulated according to
professional advice, including her psychologist;

ORDERS
that the child receive all the
health care and services she may need;

ORDERS
that the mother take an active
part in the application of the measures ordered;

ORDER
that a person working for an
establishment or body, provide aid, counsel and assistance to the child and her
family for a period of one year;

ENTRUSTS
the situation of the child X to the Director of Youth Protection to
see that the measures are carried out.
